examples.en: In summer I played ball with friends on the sandy beach.
A wide sandy beach stretches on endlessly.
Walking barefoot on the sandy beach feels good.
The children are building a sandcastle on the beach.
The sand is hot during the day, so wear slippers.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 백사장 위로 노을이 번졌어요.
examples.en: Around sunset, the glow spread over the beach.

explain: 하얀 모래가 넓게 펼쳐진 바닷가나 강가를 말해요. '해수욕장'은 사람들이 놀러 가는 장소 전체이고, 백사장은 그 안의 모래밭 자체를 가리켜요. 비슷한 말로 '모래사장'이 있어요.

phrases.en: I picked up shells on the sandy beach by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 백사장과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 모래의 색은 따로 말하지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 백사장, without specifying the color of the sand.

phrases.en: I walked along the beach in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷가 모래밭을 천천히 걷는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes slowly walking on the sand by the sea.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk on the sand beach

phrases.en: I sat on the beach and looked at the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모래 위에 앉아서 쉬는 장면에 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural for a scene of sitting and resting on the sand.

explain_en: It refers to a wide stretch of white sand by the sea or a river. '해수욕장' is the whole place people go for a beach outing, while 백사장 is the sandy area itself. A similar word is '모래사장'.

examples.ko: 길을 건너기 전에 전후좌우를 잘 살펴야 해요.
examples.en: Before crossing the road, you should look carefully in every direction.

examples.ko: 전후좌우로 흔들리는 버스에서 서 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It's hard to stand on a bus that sways back and forth and side to side.
The room was dark, so it was hard to tell directions apart.
The child looked all around, searching for his mother.
Wherever I looked, there were only high mountains all around.

examples.ko: 이 동작은 전후좌우로 한 걸음씩 움직이면 돼요.
examples.en: For this move, just step once forward, back, left and right.

explain: 앞, 뒤, 왼쪽, 오른쪽을 한꺼번에 말하는 표현이라 '사방'과 비슷해요. '전후좌우를 살피다'처럼 주변을 확인할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I check all around when driving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변을 조심해서 확인할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for carefully checking surroundings.

phrases.en: The chair moves forward, back, left and right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 네 방향으로 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes movement in all four directions.

phrases.en: It snowed, so everything all around is white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 '사방'이 더 쉽고 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but 사방 is easier and more everyday.

explain_en: It lumps together front, back, left and right, so it is close to '사방' (all sides). It is common in '전후좌우를 살피다' (look around carefully on all sides).

examples.en: The cockpit door on an airplane is locked.
The captain made an announcement from the cockpit.
The child said he wanted to look at the cockpit.
The inside of the cockpit was full of instrument panels.
The spaceship cockpit looked cool in the movie.

examples.ko: 조종실은 승객이 마음대로 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Passengers cannot enter the cockpit freely.

explain: 비행기나 배, 우주선을 조종하는 사람이 있는 방이에요. 자동차는 '운전석'이라고 하고, 승객이 앉는 곳은 '객실'이라고 해서 구분해요. 외래어 '콕핏'은 비행기나 레이싱에서 쓰는 경우가 있어요.

phrases.example: 조종실 문은 비행 중에 열지 않아요.
phrases.en: The cockpit door isn't opened during the flight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 조종실의 한 부분을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding a noun after it names a part of the cockpit.

phrases.en: The captain went into the cockpit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 들어가는 장소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 에 it marks the place being entered.

phrases.en: The captain is sitting in the pilot's seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조종실'은 방 전체이고, '조종석'은 앉는 자리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 조종실 is the whole room, while 조종석 is the seat.

explain_en: The whole room or compartment for flying or controlling. It is the room where the person who operates a plane, ship or spaceship sits. For cars you say '운전석', and the place where passengers sit is the '객실'. The loanword '콕핏' is sometimes used for planes or racing.

t90.ax: The cockpit door on an airplane is locked.

examples.ko: 산 중턱에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple halfway up the mountain.
The fog came down to the middle of the mountain.

examples.ko: 중턱쯤 올라가면 물을 마실 수 있는 곳이 나와요.
examples.en: If you climb about halfway, you will find a place to drink water.

examples.ko: 힘들어서 정상까지 못 가고 중턱에서 내려왔어요.
examples.en: It was hard, so I could not reach the top and came down from halfway.

examples.ko: 언덕 중턱에 있는 집이라서 경치가 좋아요.
examples.en: The house is on the side of a hill, so the view is nice.

examples.ko: 저기 중턱에 있는 벤치에서 잠깐 쉴까요?
examples.en: Shall we rest for a moment on the bench halfway up there?

explain: 산이나 언덕의 꼭대기와 아래 사이를 말할 때 써요. '산 중턱'처럼 산과 같이 쓰는 경우가 대부분이에요. 건물이나 책의 가운데에는 쓰지 않고 '중간'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I rested for a moment halfway up the hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산뿐 아니라 언덕에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Works for hills as well as mountains.

phrases.en: Today I climbed up to the middle of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭대기까지는 못 가고 중간까지 갔다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Implies you went only halfway, not to the top.
phrases.en_equiv: climb up to the halfway point

phrases.en: We ate our lunch boxes about halfway up the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쯤'을 붙이면 대략 그 근처라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 쯤 means roughly around that point.

explain_en: Use it for the stretch between the top and the bottom of a mountain or hill, almost always as '산 중턱'. For the middle of a building or a book, say '중간' instead.

examples.en: I shared a taxi with my friend and went home.
If we're going the same way, can we share a ride?
Sharing a ride with a stranger is a bit scary.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 옆집 사람과 합승했어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so I shared a ride with my neighbor.
If you share a ride, the taxi fare is cut in half.
Would you like to share a ride with us?

explain: '택시에 합승하다'처럼 '에'를 같이 써요. 높임은 '합승하세요', '합승하실래요?'예요. 같은 방향 사람끼리 요금을 나누려고 할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: If we're going the same way, please share the ride.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 같이 타자고 공손하게 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to invite someone to ride together.

phrases.en: I'm going to the airport too. Would you like to share a ride?
phrases.nuance_ko: 같이 타겠느냐고 부드럽게 물어볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to ask whether someone wants to ride together.
phrases.en_equiv: would you like to share a ride?

phrases.en: It's raining a lot, so I'd like to share a ride.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신이 같이 타고 싶다는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that you yourself want to ride together.
phrases.en_equiv: I'd like to share a ride

explain_en: It is used with '에', as in '택시에 합승하다'. The polite forms are '합승하세요' and '합승하실래요?'. It is common when people going the same way want to split the fare.

en: to look down on; to belittle

examples.en: You must not look down on people for their looks.
He looked down on me because I was young.
I studied hard so that no one could look down on me.
He underestimated his opponent and lost the match.
The belittling tone of voice made me feel bad.
I am upset because my friends look down on me.

explain: 깔보다는 상대가 나보다 못하다고 생각하며 낮게 볼 때 써요. '무시하다'는 상대의 말이나 존재를 신경 쓰지 않는 것이고, 깔보다는 마음속으로 낮게 보는 느낌이에요. '얕보다'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: You shouldn't look down on your opponent.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깔보다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with almost the same meaning as 깔보다.

phrases.en: Please don't look down on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 낮게 보지 말라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell someone not to look down on you.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 깔보는 눈빛으로 저를 봤어요.
phrases.en: That person looked at me with a look of contempt.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 낮게 보는 표정이나 눈을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -는 ending describes a look or expression of looking down on someone.

explain_en: Treat someone as lesser; common, spoken, somewhat blunt. 깔보다 is used when you think the other person is lower than you. '무시하다' means ignoring someone's words or existence, while 깔보다 is the inner feeling of seeing them as beneath you. '얕보다' is used in a similar way.

t90.ax: He looked down on me because I was young.

examples.en: I opened a shop with my friend as business partners.
Business partners split the profit half and half.
I'm worried because my partner and I disagree.
My longtime partner suddenly left the company.
We are partners who trust each other.

examples.ko: 동업자를 구할 때는 계약서를 꼭 써요.
examples.en: When you find a partner, be sure to write a contract.

explain: 함께 돈을 대고 일을 나누어 장사하는 사이에 써요. 월급을 받는 직원은 '동업자'가 아니고, 같은 직장 사람은 '동료'예요. 동사는 '동업하다'라서 '친구랑 동업하다'로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I run a cafe in partnership with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동업자'에서 나온 동사로, 함께 장사한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to run a business together.

phrases.en: I'm looking for a business partner to open a shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 일할 사람을 찾을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking for someone to start a business with.

phrases.en: We became business partners two years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 사업을 시작해 관계가 생긴 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes entering a business partnership.

explain_en: People in the same line of business, or partners running one. It is for people who put in money together and share the work of a business. A salaried employee is not a '동업자', and someone at the same workplace is a '동료'. The verb is '동업하다', as in '친구랑 동업하다'.

en: to let go; to send away

examples.en: Today I saw a close friend off.
I cried after sending my family off at the airport.

examples.ko: 사랑하는 사람을 떠나보내는 일은 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: Letting a loved one go is really hard.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 키운 강아지를 떠나보낸 뒤 많이 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried a lot after losing the puppy I raised for years.
It's not easy to let go of an ex.
I came on a trip to let go of the pain of the past.

explain: '보내다'는 사람이나 물건을 어디로 가게 하는 가벼운 말이고, '떠나보내다'는 가까운 사람과 헤어지거나 마음속에서 정리할 때 써서 감정이 더 커요. 세상을 떠난 사람이나 반려동물에게도 쓰고, 아픔 같은 마음을 놓아 줄 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: After letting my friend go, I cried for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤어진 뒤의 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link what happened after the parting.

phrases.en: It is so hard to let my family go.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤어지는 일이 마음 아프다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that parting is painful.

phrases.example: 이제 아픈 기억을 마음속에서 떠나보내려고 해요.
phrases.en: Now I want to let the painful memory go from my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 감정이나 기억을 정리할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for emotions or memories, not just people.
phrases.en_equiv: to let go in one's heart

explain_en: Emotional — parting with a person you care about (졸업생을 떠나보내다) 보내다 is a light word for making a person or thing go somewhere. 떠나보내다 carries more emotion, used for parting from someone close or settling something in your heart. It is also used for people or pets who have died, and figuratively for letting go of pain.

t90.ax: Today I saw a close friend off.

examples.en: A new boy moved in next door.
Maybe because he's a boy, he's really active.
I'm so busy raising two boys.
The hospital told us it's a boy.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 사내아이보다 여자아이가 더 많아요.
examples.en: In our class, there are more girls than boys.
Boys are kicking a ball in the park.

explain: '남자아이'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰지만 조금 더 예스럽고 부모 세대가 자주 써요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '남자아이'가 더 흔해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '여자아이'예요.

phrases.example: 우리 반에는 남자아이가 열 명 있어요.
phrases.en: There are ten boys in our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 말이에요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 이 말이 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning. This is more common in everyday conversation today.

phrases.en: My older sister gave birth to a baby boy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아들을 낳았다는 말을 조금 예스럽게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly old-fashioned way to say someone had a baby boy.
phrases.en_equiv: to give birth to a boy

phrases.en: The boys are kicking a ball on the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 명의 남자아이를 말할 때 복수형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The plural form, used for several boys.

explain_en: It means the same as '남자아이' but sounds a bit more old-fashioned and is used more by the parent generation. In everyday talk today, '남자아이' is more common. The counterpart is '여자아이'.

t90.ax: A new boy moved in next door.

examples.ko: 정말 죄송해요. 한 번만 용서해 주세요.
examples.en: I'm really sorry. Please forgive me just once.
My friend apologized, so I forgave him right away.
It's not easy to forgive a lie.

examples.ko: 그 사람을 용서할 마음이 아직 없어요.
examples.en: I'm not yet ready to forgive that person.
After forgiving, my heart felt at ease.
Forgiving also takes courage.

explain: '용서하다'는 잘못을 무겁게 받아들이고 마음으로 풀어 주는 느낌이에요. 가벼운 실수에는 '괜찮아요'가 자연스러워요. '봐주다'는 이번만 넘어갈 때 써서 '용서하다'보다 가벼워요.

phrases.en: I told the truth and was forgiven by my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 용서하는 쪽이 아니라 용서를 받는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person being forgiven.

phrases.en: I can't forgive that lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 화가 나서 풀어 줄 수 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is too serious to forgive.

phrases.en: I asked my friend for forgiveness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못한 사람이 진심으로 용서해 달라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person sincerely asks to be forgiven.

explain_en: Personal; forgiving someone for a wrong or mistake. '용서하다' feels weighty: taking a wrong seriously and letting it go in your heart. For small mistakes, '괜찮아요' is natural. '봐주다' means letting something slide this once and is lighter than '용서하다'.

examples.en: I call my parents every weekend to be a good child to them.
I showed my filial piety to my parents with my first paycheck.

examples.ko: 건강한 것도 부모님께 효도하는 거라고 해요.
examples.en: They say staying healthy is also a way of honoring your parents.

examples.ko: 나중에 효도하겠다고 말만 하지 말고 지금 하세요.
examples.en: Don't just say you'll be filial later; do it now.

examples.ko: 효도하고 싶은데 멀리 살아서 못 해요.
examples.en: I want to be a dutiful child, but I live far away, so I can't.
You should honor your parents while they are in good health.

explain: 효도하다는 부모님이나 어른께만 쓰고, 친구나 어린 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. '효도를 하다'로도 말하고, 대상에는 '부모님께'처럼 높임 조사 '께'를 붙이는 때가 많아요. 반대말은 '불효'예요.

phrases.example: 돈을 벌면 부모님께 효도를 하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: When I earn money, I want to be good to my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: '효도하다'와 같은 뜻으로, '을 하다'를 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, formed by adding 을 하다.

phrases.en: I want to be good to my grandmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모님이나 어른께 잘하고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express the wish to treat parents or elders well.

phrases.en: I gave my parents a gift on Parents' Day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모님께 드리는 선물을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for gifts given to one's parents.

explain_en: 효도하다 is used only toward parents or elders, never toward friends or younger people. You can also say '효도를 하다', and the target often takes the honorific particle '께', as in '부모님께'. The opposite is '불효'.

en: the symbolic meaning of a flower

examples.ko: 혹시 이 장미의 꽃말이 뭔지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you happen to know what this rose's flower meaning is?

examples.ko: 꽃을 고를 때 꽃말도 같이 봐요.
examples.en: When I choose flowers, I look at their meanings too.

examples.ko: 꽃말은 꽃 이름과 함께 외우면 쉬워요.
examples.en: Flower meanings are easy to remember along with the flower names.
I looked up the flower meanings and chose a birthday bouquet.

examples.ko: 꽃말 때문에 이 꽃은 선물하기 조심스러워요.
examples.en: Because of its flower meaning, I'm careful about giving this flower as a gift.

examples.ko: 꽃말에 대해 이야기하다가 이 가게를 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: I found this shop while talking about flower meanings.

explain: 꽃마다 따로 정해진 상징적인 뜻을 말해요. '꽃말이 뭐예요?', '꽃말이 사랑이에요'처럼 말하고, 선물할 꽃을 고를 때 자주 이야기해요. 발음은 [꼰말]이에요.

phrases.en: Every flower has its own meaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃에 정해진 뜻이 있다는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that flowers have set meanings.
phrases.en_equiv: a flower has its own meaning

phrases.en: Before giving the gift, I looked up the flower's meaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인터넷이나 책으로 뜻을 알아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking the meaning online or in a book.

phrases.en: This flower's meaning is happiness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃의 뜻을 설명할 때 쓰는 기본 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic sentence for explaining a flower's meaning.

explain_en: It is the symbolic meaning assigned to each flower. You say things like '꽃말이 뭐예요?' or '꽃말이 사랑이에요', and it comes up often when choosing flowers as gifts. It is pronounced [꼰말].

en: to scribble; to doodle; to write graffiti

examples.en: The child scribbled on the wall with crayons.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 공책에 낙서하다가 선생님께 들켰어요.
examples.en: I was scribbling in my notebook during class and the teacher noticed.
You must not doodle on the desk.

examples.ko: 심심할 때 종이에 낙서하는 걸 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like doodling on paper when I'm bored.
Someone has scribbled on the bathroom door.
I was doodling on a memo pad while on the phone.

explain: '낙서하다'는 마음대로 쓰거나 그리는 일이에요. 공책이나 종이에 하면 괜찮지만 벽이나 책상 같은 공공장소에 하면 잘못으로 여겨요. 의미 있는 그림을 그리는 '그리다'와 달리 장난스럽고 가벼운 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Please don't scribble on the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금지나 부탁을 할 때 쓰는 말로 공공장소에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for prohibitions or requests, often seen in public places.

phrases.en: I'm bored, so I'm doodling in my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심심할 때 가볍게 끄적이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes casually doodling when you have nothing to do.

phrases.example: 동생이 내 책에 낙서를 해 놓았어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling scribbled all over my book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낙서를 한 결과가 남아 있다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests the scribbles are still there as a result.

explain_en: Neutral noun-verb, random drawing, also graffiti on walls. '낙서하다' is writing or drawing freely without much purpose. On a notebook or paper it is harmless, but on walls or desks in public places it counts as misbehavior. Unlike '그리다', it feels playful and casual.

t90.ax: You must not doodle on the desk.

examples.en: As a child, I went on adventures in the mountains with friends.

examples.ko: 새로운 일에 도전하려면 가끔은 모험해야 해요.
examples.en: To take on something new, you sometimes have to take a risk.

examples.ko: 방학에 혼자 모험하는 기분으로 여행해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to travel alone over vacation with a sense of adventure.
The kids played, exploring the unfamiliar neighborhood.

examples.ko: 안전한 길보다 모험하기를 좋아하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people like adventure more than the safe path.

examples.ko: 모험할 용기가 없어서 그냥 집에 있었어요.
examples.en: I didn't have the courage to take a chance, so I just stayed home.

explain: '탐험하다'는 잘 알려지지 않은 곳을 조사하러 가는 것이고, '모험하다'는 위험을 무릅쓰고 새로운 일을 해 보는 것이에요. 명사 '모험'을 써서 '모험을 떠나다', '모험 영화'처럼 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: I set out on an adventure with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로운 곳으로 신나게 나설 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for setting out on an exciting adventure.
phrases.en_equiv: to set out on an adventure

phrases.en: Sometimes it's fine to take a risk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모험하다'와 뜻이 같지만 '모험을 하다'가 말할 때 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '모험하다', but often sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.en: I watched an adventure movie on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모험'을 다른 말 앞에 붙여 이야기의 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '모험' placed before another noun names a kind of story.

explain_en: '탐험하다' is going to explore places little known, while '모험하다' is taking a risk to try something new. The noun '모험' is used a lot, as in '모험을 떠나다' (set off on an adventure) and '모험 영화' (adventure movie).

examples.en: My grandmother put a charm in my bag.

examples.ko: 이 부적은 시험 잘 보라고 받은 거예요.
examples.en: I got this charm to do well on the exam.

examples.ko: 지갑 속 부적이 행운을 가져다줄 거예요.
examples.en: The charm in my wallet will bring luck.
I bought a charm at the temple.

examples.ko: 부적처럼 항상 그 반지를 끼고 다녀요.
examples.en: I always wear that ring like a lucky charm.

examples.ko: 차에 부적을 걸어 두는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people hang a charm in their car.

explain: 원래는 종이에 글씨나 그림을 그려 몸에 지니는 물건이에요. 요즘은 '행운의 물건'이라는 뜻으로도 말해요. 같은 발음인 '부적당하다'의 '부적'과는 관계없어요.

phrases.en: I stuck a charm on the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 문에 부적을 둘 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when placing a charm on a house or door.

phrases.en: This key ring is my lucky charm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종이가 아니라 행운을 주는 물건에도 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for lucky objects that aren't paper charms.

phrases.example: 그는 늘 작은 부적을 지니고 다녀요.
phrases.en: He always carries a small charm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 가지고 다닌다는 뜻이에요. '가지고 다니다'보다 조금 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to keep it on oneself. A bit more formal than 가지고 다니다.

explain_en: Traditionally it is paper with writing or a drawing that you carry on your body for luck or protection. People today also use it loosely for any lucky object. It has nothing to do with the 부적 inside 부적당하다 (unsuitable).
